relevance_note: Single-centre thalidomide cohort of 16 monogenic AID patients including four with Blau syndrome, each with an individual NOD2 variant, sex, age and features in Additional file 2 (e.g. 'Blau syndrome | NOD2: p. R587C').
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON and cut spans as exact prefixes of the supplementary table rows (Additional file 2) and Table 2 rows, then every span was checked verbatim. In scope: patients No. 4-7 (Blau syndrome, NOD2). The other 12 cohort patients (other genes/diseases) get no rows; cohort size 16. Labels: the 'No.' column holds bare numbers, but the text calls patients 'Case 1', 'Cases 4 and 6', 'cases 5 and 12', 'cases 6 and 14'; rule 1 applied as 'Case <n>'. Case 7 is never named in the text, so 'Case 7' extends the paper's own labelling scheme (alternative would be 'Table 2 #7'). Age at baseline (start of thalidomide; 8.67, 5.0, 8.75, 10.83 years) is not an age at onset, diagnosis or last evaluation, so those fields are 'not reported'; the follow-up lasted up to 12 months after baseline. Variant for No. 5 is printed 'p.481G\>D' in the Markdown (backslash is a Markdown escape); value recorded as 'p.481G>D', protein notation without a reference amino acid, exactly as printed otherwise. No zygosity, inheritance, transcript or classification given for any NOD2 variant. Table 1 gives only per-disease counts (e.g. Fever 1, Elevated CRP 3, Joint involvement 2 among Blau patients) without names, so they were not assigned to individuals. Table 2 for Blau patients gives the number of active arthritis episodes (note ^b); Cases 4 and 6 have 0 throughout and the text says they 'had persistent inactive arthritis', which may imply a history of arthritis, so 'active arthritis' is excluded for them while the checklist item 'arthritis or joint synovitis' is left not reported. Active uveitis/ophthalmia is excluded by two group statements naming the group, while each Blau patient has 'uveitis' listed in the supplement (history vs current activity, not treated as a contradiction); checklist uveitis is observed. Peripheral neuropathy and somnolence excluded as adverse events from 'None of the patients had adverse events...'; this narrower absence does not exclude the checklist item 'cranial or other neuropathy (facial palsy)'. Neuropathy and liver dysfunction as exclusion criteria were not used. Cardiac findings (left atrial enlargement, pericardial effusion, coronary arteries widened) recorded as stated; not mapped to pericarditis or vasculitis. Thalidomide treatment for each person rests on the statement that all 16 study patients were given thalidomide. Table 2 shows '-' after 3 months for Cases 5 and 7 (and the text says four patients discontinued after 3 months) but does not define '-', so discontinuation was not recorded for them individually. is_proband left null (cohort paper, no proband wording). Supplementary file 1 (disease-activity scoring) has no patient data.
